questions.question: Which of the following is the correct statement about the Rajya Sabha?

options.text: All the members are directly elected by the people.
It is known as the Council of the States.
It is known as the lower house of the parliament.
The term of the members is for 5 years.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is known as the Council of the States**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rajya Sabha is also known as the Council of States, representing the states and union territories of India.
 
• Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies and by the members of the Electoral college for Union Territories, using a single transferable vote.
 
• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution; however, one-third of its members retire every two years.
 
• The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Term of Members:** Each member of the Rajya Sabha serves a term of six years, with one-third of the members retiring every two years.
 
• **Composition:** The Rajya Sabha can have a maximum of 250 members, out of which 12 are nominated by the President of India for their contributions to art, literature, science, and social services.
 
• **Role and Powers:** The Rajya Sabha has legislative powers, but it cannot initiate or amend money bills. However, it can suggest amendments to money bills, which the Lok Sabha may or may not accept.
 
• **Sessions:** The Rajya Sabha meets in continuous sessions, and unlike the Lok Sabha, it is not subject to dissolution.
 
• **Special Powers:** The Rajya Sabha can authorize the Parliament to legislate on a subject from the State List if it is deemed to be of national importance, by passing a resolution with a two-thirds majority.

questions.question: Rabindranath Tagore referred to __________ as Nritya Samragini, which translates to 'the empress of dance'.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sitara Devi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rabindranath Tagore referred to Sitara Devi as **Nritya Samragini**, which translates to 'the empress of dance'.
 
• Sitara Devi was a renowned Indian dancer of the **classical Kathak style**.
 
• She was known for her **energetic style and innovative choreography** in Kathak.
 
• Sitara Devi was awarded the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** and the **Padma Shri** for her contributions to Indian dance.
 
• Her performances were acclaimed both **nationally and internationally**, inspiring many generations of dancers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak Dance**

 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• It originated from the traveling bards of North India known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• The dance form emphasizes intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures and facial expressions.
 
• Kathak has a strong connection with the **Bhakti Movement** and the **Mughal courts**, where it evolved as a court entertainment.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**
 
 
• This is the highest Indian recognition given to practicing artists.
 
• The award is given by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama**.
 
• It was established in 1952 and recognizes outstanding achievement in the performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Padma Shri**
 
 
• Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in India.
 
• It is awarded for distinguished service in various fields including the arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
• The award was instituted in 1954 and is announced annually on Republic Day.
 
 
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore**
 
 
• Rabindranath Tagore was a Bengali polymath who reshaped Bengali literature and music, as well as Indian art, in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• He became the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
 
• Tagore's poetry, short stories, and novels are widely celebrated and translated into many languages worldwide.

questions.question: The term 'Aus', 'Aman' and 'Boro' are associated with which crop in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Paddy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The terms 'Aus', 'Aman', and 'Boro' refer to different cropping seasons for paddy cultivation in India.
 
• 'Aus' is the pre-monsoon crop, typically sown in April-May and harvested in July-August.
 
• 'Aman' is the monsoon crop, usually sown in June-July and harvested in November-December.
 
• 'Boro' is the winter crop, planted in November-December and harvested in April-May.
 
• These terms help farmers plan their cultivation cycles based on climatic conditions and water availability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paddy Cultivation:** Paddy is primarily grown in regions with abundant water supply, such as river deltas and coastal areas.
 
• **Irrigation:** Efficient irrigation systems are crucial for paddy farming, especially during the 'Boro' season.
 
• **Rice Varieties:** India is home to a diverse range of rice varieties, each suited to different climatic conditions.
 
• **Climate Impact:** Climate change impacts paddy cultivation, affecting the timing and yield of crops.
 
• **Economic Importance:** Paddy is a staple food crop in India, playing a vital role in food security and the economy.

questions.question: How many chances does a high jumper get for overcoming a certain height?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three chances**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In high jump competitions, athletes are typically given **three chances** to clear a specific height.
 
• A failed attempt is recorded if the jumper dislodges the bar or makes a foul jump.
 
• If the jumper clears the height on any of the three attempts, they progress to the next height.
 
• Three consecutive failed attempts at any height result in elimination from the competition.
 
• These rules apply to most standard high jump competitions, including those governed by the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High Jump Technique**

 
 
• The Fosbury Flop is the most common technique used by high jumpers today.
 
• It involves a curved approach and a backward layout over the bar.
 
 
 
• **Equipment**
 
 
• High jumpers use a fiberglass or carbon fiber crossbar for competition.
 
• Mats or crash pads are used for safety upon landing.
 
 
 
• **Record Holders**
 
 
• The men's world record for high jump is held by Javier Sotomayor of Cuba with a jump of 2.45 meters.
 
• The women's world record is held by Stefka Kostadinova of Bulgaria with a jump of 2.09 meters.
 
 
 
• **Competition Rules**
 
 
• A fair jump is when the jumper clears the bar without knocking it off the supports.
 
• Jumpers must take off from one foot.
 
• Competitions are often governed by the rules of the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF).

questions.question: The Iron Age site named Tekwada is located in _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tekwada is an Iron Age site located in the state of **Maharashtra**, India.
 
• The site is known for its archaeological significance related to the **Iron Age**.
 
• Excavations at Tekwada have revealed artifacts such as pottery, tools, and remnants of ancient structures.
 
• It provides valuable insights into the lifestyle and technological advancements of ancient populations in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron Age**:

 
 
• The Iron Age is a prehistoric period following the Bronze Age, marked by the widespread use of iron for tools and weapons.
 
• It began around 1200 BCE and lasted until the advent of written history in various regions.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Sites in Maharashtra**:
 
 
• Maharashtra is home to several significant archaeological sites, including Ajanta and Ellora Caves, known for their ancient rock-cut architecture and paintings.
 
• Other notable sites include the Karla and Bhaja Caves, which provide insights into early Buddhist architecture.
 
 
 
• **Pottery in Iron Age**:
 
 
• Pottery was a major artifact found at Iron Age sites, reflecting the technological and artistic capabilities of the era.
 
• Different types of pottery, such as black and red ware, have been discovered, indicating diverse cultural practices.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Excavations**:
 
 
• Excavations help in uncovering historical artifacts and structures, providing a window into ancient civilizations.
 
• They are crucial for understanding the development of human societies and their technological advancements.

questions.question: Which Census decade recorded the highest population growth rate (in terms of percentage) in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: 1961-1971**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The decade 1961-1971 recorded the highest population growth rate in India, with a growth rate of 24.8%.
 
• During this period, India saw significant demographic changes and a substantial increase in population.
 
• This growth rate was influenced by various factors, including improvements in healthcare, reduction in mortality rates, and better living conditions.
 
• The population growth rate during 1961-1971 was higher compared to the subsequent decades.
 
• Sources: Census of India, Ministry of Home Affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census of India:** The Census of India is conducted every 10 years and provides comprehensive data on the country's population, housing, and various demographic factors.
 
• **Population Growth Rate:** It refers to the percentage change in the population over a specific period, often influenced by birth rates, death rates, and migration.
 
• **Demographic Transition:** India has undergone demographic transition, moving from high birth and death rates to lower birth and death rates, contributing to changes in population growth.
 
• **Healthcare Improvements:** The increase in population growth during 1961-1971 was partly due to advancements in medical facilities and healthcare services, reducing mortality rates.
 
• **Economic and Social Development:** Improved economic conditions, better sanitation, and access to education also played a role in the population increase during this period.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**William Jones**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sir William Jones, a British philologist and orientalist, founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784.
 
• The establishment aimed to promote Oriental studies, including the study of Indian languages, literature, and culture.
 
• The society was created in Calcutta (now Kolkata), which was then the capital of British India.
 
• William Jones is renowned for his work in comparative linguistics and for proposing the existence of a relationship among European and Indian languages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asiatic Society of Bengal:**

 
 
• The society's official name at its inception was "Asiatick Society."
 
• It played a pivotal role in the development of Indology and the study of Asian cultures and histories.
 
• The society published a journal called "Asiatic Researches," which disseminated knowledge about Asian civilizations.
 
• Over time, the Asiatic Society contributed significantly to the preservation and dissemination of ancient Indian manuscripts and texts.
 
 
 
• **William Jones:**
 
 
• He was born on September 28, 1746, and died on April 27, 1794.
 
• Jones was a pioneer in the study of Sanskrit and is known for his translations of ancient Indian texts.
 
• He proposed the existence of a Proto-Indo-European language, showing connections between Latin, Greek, and Sanskrit.
 
• His work laid the foundation for modern comparative linguistics.
 
 
 
• **Indology:**
 
 
• Indology is the academic study of the history, cultures, languages, and literature of India and the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Indologists study ancient texts, inscriptions, and other historical materials to understand India's past.
 
• The field encompasses various disciplines, including archaeology, history, and philology.
 
• Prominent Indologists include Max Müller, A.L. Basham, and R.G. Bhandarkar.

questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights entails trafficking of human beings and forced labour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rights against Exploitation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rights against Exploitation is enshrined in Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 23 explicitly prohibits trafficking of human beings, begar (forced labor), and other similar forms of forced labor.
 
• Article 24 prohibits employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or any other hazardous employment.
 
• These rights ensure the protection of individuals from being exploited and abused in any form.
 
• The enforcement of these rights is crucial to maintaining human dignity and freedom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trafficking of Human Beings:** Involves the illegal trade of humans for purposes such as forced labor, sexual slavery, or commercial exploitation.
 
• **Begar:** A form of forced labor without payment, often practiced as a social norm in historical contexts.
 
• **Hazardous Employment:** Work that poses a risk to physical health, safety, and well-being, such as in factories or mines.
 
• **Child Labor Laws:** Govern the working conditions and permissible work types for children, aiming to protect their rights and education.
 
• **Human Dignity:** A fundamental principle ensuring respect and ethical treatment of individuals, safeguarded by various human rights legislations.

questions.question: The weaker warm storms that grow stronger over time are finally converted into huge storms or hurricanes. Which of the following climate regions is the origin of such hurricanes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical climate region**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hurricanes primarily form in the tropical climate regions due to warm ocean waters and favorable atmospheric conditions.
 
• The tropical climate region provides consistent heat and humidity, crucial for the development and intensification of hurricanes.
 
• Most hurricanes originate in the Atlantic Ocean, particularly in the area known as the hurricane belt, which lies within the tropical climate region.
 
• The warm sea surface temperatures in the tropics, generally above 26.5°C, provide the energy needed for hurricanes to form and strengthen.
 
• Regions such as the Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, and the western Atlantic Ocean are common origins for hurricanes, all of which are situated in the tropical climate zone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tropical Cyclones**

 
 
• These are large-scale storm systems with a well-defined center and are characterized by strong winds and heavy rain.
 
• The term "hurricane" is used in the Atlantic and Northeast Pacific, while "typhoon" is used in the Northwest Pacific, and "cyclone" in the South Pacific and Indian Ocean.
 
 
 
• **Formation Factors**
 
 
• Six main factors are necessary for the formation of hurricanes: warm ocean waters, atmospheric instability, high humidity, Coriolis force, a pre-existing disturbance, and low vertical wind shear.
 
 
 
• **Hurricane Season**
 
 
• The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 to November 30, with the peak occurring between mid-August and late October.
 
 
 
• **Impact Zones**
 
 
• Regions most affected by hurricanes include the southeastern United States, the Caribbean, Central America, and parts of East Asia.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change**
 
 
• Climate change is believed to influence the frequency and intensity of hurricanes, with warmer oceans potentially leading to more powerful and wetter storms.

questions.question: The author of the Hindi novel 'Kohre Mein Kaid Rang' is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Govind Mishra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Govind Mishra is a celebrated Hindi novelist known for his profound literary works.
 
• He was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1998 for his novel "Lal Peeli Zameen".
 
• Govind Mishra has authored more than 50 books, including novels, short stories, and essays.
 
• His writing often explores themes of human struggles and social changes in contemporary India.
 
• "Kohre Mein Kaid Rang" is one of his notable works that reflect his narrative prowess and deep understanding of human emotions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sahitya Akademi Award:**

 
 
• It is a literary honor in India which is awarded annually by Sahitya Akademi, India's National Academy of Letters.
 
• The award recognizes outstanding works of literary merit in the 24 Indian languages recognized by the Akademi.
 
• It was established in 1954 and is one of the most prestigious literary awards in India.
 
• Recipients of the award receive a cash prize and an inscribed copper plaque.
 
 
 
• **Hindi Literature:**
 
 
• Hindi literature has a rich history dating back to the medieval period with works like "Ramcharitmanas" by Tulsidas.
 
• Modern Hindi literature began in the 19th century with the advent of social and literary reforms.
 
• Prominent figures include Munshi Premchand, Mahadevi Verma, and Harivansh Rai Bachchan.
 
• Contemporary Hindi literature continues to evolve, addressing current social issues and changes.
 
 
 
• **Govind Mishra's Contributions:**
 
 
• Besides novels, Govind Mishra has written numerous essays and short stories.
 
• His works have been translated into several Indian languages, broadening their reach and impact.
 
• He has also been involved in literary criticism and has contributed to the academic discourse on Hindi literature.
 
• Govind Mishra's writings often reflect his concern for the marginalized sections of society.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Bissu Mela organised to thank Santoora Devi for the good harvest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bissu Mela is a traditional festival celebrated in Uttarakhand.
 
• The festival is organized to thank Santoora Devi for a bountiful harvest.
 
• Bissu Mela is celebrated primarily in the Jaunsar-Bawar region of Uttarakhand.
 
• The festival marks the beginning of the harvest season and is an important cultural event for the local community.
 
• People participate in various cultural activities, including traditional dances and songs, during the mela.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jaunsar-Bawar Region:** This region is known for its distinct cultural heritage and traditions, located in the Dehradun district of Uttarakhand.
 
• **Santoora Devi:** Santoora Devi is a revered deity in the region, and the Bissu Mela is organized to honor her and seek blessings for a good harvest.
 
• **Traditional Attire:** During the Bissu Mela, people dress in their traditional attire, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of the area.
 
• **Folk Dances and Songs:** The mela features various folk dances and songs, which are integral to the celebration and reflect the local customs and traditions.
 
• **Harvest Festivals in India:** Similar to Bissu Mela, other harvest festivals in India include Pongal in Tamil Nadu, Baisakhi in Punjab, and Makar Sankranti in various parts of the country.

questions.question: In June 2022, Eknath Sambhaji Shinde became the Chief Minister of which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Eknath Shinde was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Maharashtra on June 30, 2022.
 
• He succeeded Uddhav Thackeray, who resigned following a political crisis in the state.
 
• Eknath Shinde is a senior leader of the Shiv Sena party.
 
• He has previously served as the Cabinet Minister of Urban Development and Public Works (Public Undertakings) in the Maharashtra Government.
 
• The Deputy Chief Minister, Devendra Fadnavis, was also sworn in on the same day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shiv Sena Party**

 
 
• Founded in 1966 by Bal Thackeray, it is a right-wing Marathi regional political party.
 
• The party's primary base is in the state of Maharashtra.
 
• Shiv Sena advocates for the rights of the Marathi people and promotes the use of Marathi language.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra Political Crisis 2022**
 
 
• The political turmoil began when Eknath Shinde led a faction of Shiv Sena MLAs to rebel against Uddhav Thackeray's leadership.
 
• This led to Uddhav Thackeray's resignation as Chief Minister on June 29, 2022.
 
 
 
• **Devendra Fadnavis**
 
 
• He is a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
 
• Previously served as the Chief Minister of Maharashtra from 2014 to 2019.
 
• Currently, he serves as the Deputy Chief Minister under Eknath Shinde's leadership.
 
 
 
• **Urban Development in Maharashtra**
 
 
• Maharashtra is one of India's most urbanized states, with Mumbai being the financial capital of the country.
 
• The state government focuses on infrastructure development, housing, and public transportation to support urban growth.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: Who among the following founded the 'Satyashodhak Samaj' in 1873?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyotiba Phule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jyotiba Phule founded the 'Satyashodhak Samaj' in 1873 in Maharashtra.
 
• The organization aimed to eliminate social discrimination and promote equal rights for lower castes.
 
• Satyashodhak Samaj translates to "Society of Truth Seekers."
 
• Phule's initiative was pivotal in advocating for education and social reforms, especially for women and lower castes.
 
• The movement emphasized rational thinking and opposed the caste system and religious orthodoxy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jyotiba Phule**

 
 
• Born on April 11, 1827, in Maharashtra, Jyotiba Phule was a prominent social reformer, thinker, and writer.
 
• He and his wife Savitribai Phule started the first school for girls in Pune in 1848.
 
• Phule wrote several books, including "Gulamgiri" (Slavery), highlighting the plight of lower castes and advocating for their rights.
 
• He is often referred to as the 'Father of Indian Social Revolution' for his efforts in fighting caste discrimination and promoting education.
 
 
 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj's Impact**
 
 
• The organization played a crucial role in the social awakening of lower castes in Maharashtra and other parts of India.
 
• It laid the foundation for subsequent social reform movements and the rise of Dalit activism in India.
 
• The principles of Satyashodhak Samaj inspired many future leaders, including Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms of the 19th Century**
 
 
• The 19th century in India saw a wave of social reform movements aimed at eradicating social evils like caste discrimination, child marriage, and sati.
 
• Other notable reformers of the era include Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, and Swami Dayananda Saraswati.
 
 
 
• **Education and Social Change**
 
 
• Education was seen as a powerful tool for social change and empowerment during the 19th century.
 
• Reformers like Phule emphasized the need for educating women and lower castes to break the cycle of oppression and poverty.

questions.question: Which type of loan is supported by MUDRA?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-farm loan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) supports loans to non-farm sector income-generating activities.
 
• It aims to promote micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector, including manufacturing, trading, and services.
 
• Loans under MUDRA are categorized into three products: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh).
 
• MUDRA loans are provided through various financial institutions like banks, NBFCs, and MFIs.
 
• The initiative helps in providing credit to micro and small enterprises that are often excluded from the formal banking sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MUDRA Yojana:** Launched in April 2015 by the Government of India to provide financial support to non-farm small/micro enterprises.
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY):** Under this scheme, MUDRA provides refinance support to banks/NBFCs/MFIs for lending to micro units.
 
• **Credit Guarantee Fund:** The Government has set up a Credit Guarantee Fund for MUDRA loans to reduce the risk for lending institutions.
 
• **Employment Generation:** MUDRA loans aim at generating self-employment opportunities and promoting entrepreneurship.
 
• **Non-Farm Sector:** Includes activities such as small manufacturing units, shopkeepers, fruits/vegetable vendors, truck operators, food-service units, repair shops, machine operators, small industries, artisans, food processors, etc.

questions.question: What is the percentage of 's' character in the carbon atom of acetylene?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Acetylene, also known as ethyne, has the chemical formula C₂H₂.
 
• Each carbon atom in acetylene forms two sigma (σ) bonds and two pi (π) bonds.
 
• In acetylene, the bonding involves sp hybridization for carbon atoms.
 
• Sp hybridization implies that each carbon atom has 50% s-character and 50% p-character in its hybrid orbitals.
 
• Therefore, the percentage of s-character in the carbon atom of acetylene is 50%, which corresponds to the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acetylene**: A colorless gas used as a fuel and a chemical building block.
 
• **Hybridization**: The concept of mixing atomic orbitals to form new hybrid orbitals suitable for the pairing of electrons to form chemical bonds.
 
• **Sigma Bond (σ bond)**: A single covalent bond formed by the direct overlap of atomic orbitals, resulting in a region of electron density along the axis connecting the two bonded nuclei.
 
• **Pi Bond (π bond)**: A type of covalent bond that results from the sideways overlap of p orbitals, which creates regions of electron density above and below the axis of the bonded atoms.
 
• **Sp Hybridization**: A type of orbital hybridization where one s orbital and one p orbital mix to form two equivalent sp hybrid orbitals, each having 50% s-character and 50% p-character.

questions.question: In Union Budget 2023, a sub-scheme of which of the following Yojanas has been proposed with the investment of ₹6,000 crore to enable activities of fishermen, fish vendors and micro and small enterprises?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PM Matsya Sampada Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In Union Budget 2023, the government proposed a sub-scheme under PM Matsya Sampada Yojana with an investment of ₹6,000 crore.
 
• This investment aims to support activities related to fishermen, fish vendors, and micro and small enterprises.
 
• The PM Matsya Sampada Yojana focuses on sustainable development of India's fisheries sector.
 
• It seeks to enhance fish production and productivity through modern technology and infrastructure.
 
• The scheme addresses critical gaps in the value chain including infrastructure, modernization, and traceability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)**

 
 
• Launched in May 2020 with a budget allocation of ₹20,050 crore.
 
• Aims to double fish production and export earnings, and generate employment by 2024-25.
 
• Focuses on enhancing fish production, improving infrastructure, and ensuring sustainable fisheries management.
 
• Includes components like fishery development, aquaculture, post-harvest infrastructure, and fish marketing systems.
 
• It is part of the Blue Revolution initiative for the growth and development of the fisheries sector in India.
 
 
 
• **PM Fasal Bima Yojana**
 
 
• Launched in 2016 to provide insurance coverage and financial support to farmers in the event of crop failure.
 
• Covers risks like drought, flood, pest attacks, and other natural calamities.
 
• Premium rates are subsidized by the government to make it affordable for farmers.
 
• Ensures rapid claim settlement for farmers to recover losses and continue farming activities.
 
 
 
• **PM Ujjwala Yojana**
 
 
• Launched in 2016 to provide free LPG connections to women from BPL households.
 
• Aims to reduce health hazards associated with cooking using traditional fuels.
 
• Promotes the use of clean energy and improves the quality of life for women and their families.
 
• Over 8 crore LPG connections have been distributed under this scheme.
 
 
 
• **PM Mudra Yojana**
 
 
• Launched in 2015 to provide loans up to ₹10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.
 
• Focuses on promoting entrepreneurship and generating employment.
 
• Offers three types of loans: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh).
 
• Helps small businesses and startups to access credit and grow their operations.

questions.question: India launched the 'National Social Assistance Programme' in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1995**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) was launched by the Government of India in August 1995.
 
• It aims to provide financial assistance to the elderly, widows, and persons with disabilities in the form of social pensions.
 
• NSAP is a centrally sponsored scheme that comes under the Ministry of Rural Development.
 
• The programme includes schemes like the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS), and Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS).
 
• The NSAP aims to ensure minimum national standards for social assistance in addition to the benefits that states are currently providing or might provide in the future.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)**

 
 
• This scheme provides a monthly pension to elderly individuals who are 60 years or older and belong to below poverty line (BPL) households.
 
• As of recent guidelines, the central government provides Rs. 200 per month for beneficiaries aged 60-79 years and Rs. 500 per month for those aged 80 years and above.
 
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS)**
 
 
• Under this scheme, widows aged 40-59 years and belonging to BPL households receive a monthly pension of Rs. 300 from the central government.
 
• Many states provide additional amounts on top of the central contribution.
 
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS)**
 
 
• This scheme is designed for individuals aged 18-59 years with severe disabilities and belonging to BPL households.
 
• The central government provides Rs. 300 per month, and states may add more to this amount.
 
 
 
• **Annapurna Scheme**
 
 
• The Annapurna Scheme provides 10 kg of free food grains per month to BPL senior citizens who are not covered under IGNOAPS.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria**
 
 
• The primary eligibility criteria for all NSAP schemes are that the beneficiaries must belong to BPL households.
 
• State governments are responsible for identifying and verifying the beneficiaries under these schemes.

questions.question: Which of the following Mughal emperors issued silver coins in the honour of his wife Mehrunnisa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jahangir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mughal Emperor Jahangir issued silver coins in honor of his beloved wife, Mehrunnisa, who was also known as Nur Jahan.
 
• These coins were unique as they carried the name of the queen, which was an uncommon practice in Mughal coinage.
 
• Nur Jahan was a powerful influence in Jahangir's court and had a significant role in administrative matters.
 
• The coins symbolized Jahangir's deep affection and respect for Nur Jahan, highlighting her prominence in the Mughal empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nur Jahan**

 
 
• Born as Mehrunnisa, she was the twentieth and most beloved wife of Emperor Jahangir.
 
• She was a highly educated and influential woman, known for her administrative acumen and architectural patronage.
 
• Nur Jahan effectively wielded power and was one of the few Mughal women who left a significant mark on the empire's history.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Coinage**
 
 
• Mughal coinage was known for its artistic excellence and intricate designs.
 
• Coins issued by Jahangir often depicted his interest in various arts and his deep affection for Nur Jahan.
 
 
 
• **Jahangir's Reign**
 
 
• Jahangir ruled from 1605 to 1627 and was known for his patronage of the arts.
 
• His reign was marked by a relatively stable administration and flourishing cultural activities.
 
 
 
• **Role of Women in Mughal Empire**
 
 
• Women like Nur Jahan played crucial roles in the Mughal court, influencing politics and culture.
 
• Their contributions were often commemorated through various means, including coinage and architecture.

questions.question: To which of the following groups do whales belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mammalia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Whales are classified under the class **Mammalia**, which includes all mammals.
 
• Unlike fish, whales are warm-blooded and have lungs for breathing air.
 
• Whales give birth to live young and nurse them with milk produced by mammary glands.
 
• They have a layer of blubber under their skin for insulation in cold water environments.
 
• The order **Cetacea** encompasses all whales, dolphins, and porpoises.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mammalia Characteristics**

 
 
• Mammals have three middle ear bones and hair or fur at some stage of their life cycle.
 
• They possess a neocortex, a region of the brain involved in higher-order brain functions.
 
• Mammals have a diaphragm that assists in breathing.
 
 
 
• **Cetacea Order**
 
 
• The order Cetacea is divided into two suborders: Mysticeti (baleen whales) and Odontoceti (toothed whales).
 
• Members of this order are exclusively aquatic and are adapted to life in water.
 
 
 
• **Adaptations of Whales**
 
 
• Whales have streamlined bodies and modified limbs (flippers) for efficient swimming.
 
• They possess a thick layer of blubber for energy storage and insulation.
 
• Whales have specialized respiratory systems to hold their breath for extended periods.
 
 
 
• **Whale Conservation**
 
 
• Many whale species are endangered due to threats like hunting, pollution, and climate change.
 
• International efforts and regulations like the International Whaling Commission aim to protect whale populations.

questions.question: Buddhadev Dasgupta was a famous instrumentalist of which of the following instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarod**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Buddhadev Dasgupta** was a celebrated Indian classical musician known for his mastery over the **Sarod**.
 
• He was a prominent disciple of the **Shahjahanpur Gharana** of Sarod playing.
 
• Dasgupta was awarded the prestigious **Padma Bhushan** by the Government of India in recognition of his contribution to Indian classical music.
 
• He was also a recipient of the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**, which is one of the highest Indian recognitions given to practicing artists.
 
• His playing style is noted for its lyrical and expressive qualities, blending traditional elements with innovative techniques.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarod:**

 
 
• The Sarod is a stringed instrument used mainly in Indian classical music.
 
• It is known for its deep, weighty, introspective sound, unlike the sitar which has a lighter and more resonant tone.
 
• The Sarod is fretless, allowing the musician to slide between notes smoothly.
 
 
 
• **Shahjahanpur Gharana:**
 
 
• This Gharana is one of the principal schools of Sarod playing in India.
 
• It was founded by Ustad Murad Ali Khan in the 19th century.
 
• The style is characterized by its emphasis on both melody and rhythm.
 
 
 
• **Padma Bhushan:**
 
 
• It is the third-highest civilian award in the Republic of India.
 
• Established on 2 January 1954, it is awarded for distinguished service of a high order in any field.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award:**
 
 
• This award is given by Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance & Drama.
 
• It is the highest Indian recognition given to practicing artists.

questions.question:
Anorexia Nervosa is an eating disorder characterised by ________.

 a) an abnormally heavy body weight

 b) an intense fear of losing weight

 c) a distorted perception of weight

 d) trying to lose weight by exercising excessively
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**c and d**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Anorexia Nervosa is characterized by a **distorted perception of weight** and body image, where individuals see themselves as overweight despite being underweight.
 
• Individuals with Anorexia Nervosa often engage in **excessive exercise, extreme dieting, and other behaviors to lose weight**.
 
• This disorder involves an **intense fear of gaining weight** and a persistent behavior to avoid weight gain.
 
• People suffering from this condition may have a **low body mass index (BMI)** due to restricted food intake.
 
• Anorexia Nervosa can lead to severe health complications, including **malnutrition, bone loss, and heart problems**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eating Disorders:** A range of psychological disorders characterized by abnormal or disturbed eating habits, including Anorexia Nervosa, Bulimia Nervosa, and Binge Eating Disorder.
 
• **Body Dysmorphic Disorder:** A mental health condition where a person spends a lot of time worrying about flaws in their appearance, which are often unnoticeable to others.
 
• **DSM-5 Criteria:** The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, outlines specific criteria for diagnosing Anorexia Nervosa, including restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, intense fear of gaining weight, and disturbance in the way one's body weight or shape is experienced.
 
• **Health Risks:** Anorexia Nervosa can lead to severe physical health issues, such as electrolyte imbalances, cardiovascular complications, osteoporosis, and amenorrhea.
 
• **Treatment Options:** Include psychotherapy, nutritional counseling, medical monitoring, and sometimes medications to address underlying mental health issues.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a physiographic division of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Tibetan Plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The physiographic divisions of India primarily include The Himalayan Mountains, The Peninsular Plateau, The Northern Plains, The Coastal Plains, and The Islands.
 
• The Tibetan Plateau is located to the north of the Himalayan Mountains and is not considered part of India's physiographic divisions.
 
• The Tibetan Plateau, often referred to as "the Roof of the World," is the highest and largest plateau in the world, mainly covering regions in China and parts of India.
 
• India's physiographic divisions are based on distinct geological structures and landscapes, which the Tibetan Plateau does not form part of.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Himalayan Mountains**

 
 
• They are the youngest and highest mountain range in the world, stretching across the northern boundary of India.
 
• They consist of three parallel ranges: the Greater Himalayas, the Lesser Himalayas, and the Outer Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **The Peninsular Plateau**
 
 
• This is a large plateau in southern India, forming the oldest and most stable part of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It is divided into two main parts: the Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **The Northern Plains**
 
 
• These plains are formed by the alluvial deposits of the Indus, Ganges, and Brahmaputra rivers.
 
• They extend across the northern part of India and are known for their fertile soil and dense population.
 
 
 
• **The Coastal Plains**
 
 
• They are located along the eastern and western coasts of India, known as the Eastern Coastal Plains and Western Coastal Plains respectively.
 
• These plains are characterized by their rich biodiversity and significant economic activities like agriculture and fishing.

questions.question: In Harappan civilisation, cities were planned with the streets generally oriented along the ________ directions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cardinal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Harappan civilization, also known as the Indus Valley Civilization, was noted for its advanced urban planning.
 
• Cities in the Harappan civilization were planned with streets oriented along the cardinal directions, i.e., North-South and East-West.
 
• This alignment facilitated efficient drainage systems and optimized the use of sunlight and wind.
 
• The layout of streets and buildings indicates a high level of knowledge in geometry and urban planning.
 
• Major cities like Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa exhibit this meticulous planning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cardinal Directions**

 
 
• The four main points of a compass: North, South, East, and West.
 
• Used in navigation and mapping for orientation and to determine direction.
 
 
 
• **Urban Planning in Harappan Civilization**
 
 
• Included well-organized streets and sophisticated drainage systems.
 
• Homes were built with uniformity, often with baked bricks.
 
• The cities also had granaries, warehouses, and public baths.
 
 
 
• **Drainage Systems**
 
 
• Harappan cities had advanced drainage systems, with covered drains running along the main streets.
 
• Each house was connected to the main drainage system.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Findings**
 
 
• Excavations at Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, and other sites have revealed evidence of planned urban layouts and infrastructure.
 
• Artifacts such as seals, pottery, and tools provide insights into the daily life and trade practices of the Harappan people.
